column1: # HOTD2 function names — the committed source of truth for the Ghidra database.
# Addresses are virtual, lower-case hex, no 0x prefix.
# Regenerate from a live database with:   ./ghidra/run.sh export-annotations
# Replay onto a fresh import with:        ./ghidra/run.sh apply-annotations
# ApplyAnnotations only renames a symbol whose current name is still a Ghidra
# default (FUN_/SUB_/LAB_/DAT_/UNK_), so re-applying is idempotent and never
# clobbers a name a human chose in the GUI.
# Names recovered by Ghidra's own analysers (CRT, D3DX, Catch@/Unwind@) are
# deliberately NOT listed: auto-analysis recreates them on import.

column3: walks the region tables; the engine's only table-driven draw path
matrix -> (rx, ry, rz) BAMS decomposition
writes {float x,y,z; int rx,ry,rz}; Ghidra types all six as float and is wrong
consumes the shot-test list, per player
sets obj+0x34 |= 8 and the shooter bit
writes BAMS pitch/yaw; yaw = atan2(dx, dz)

Appends the actor to the per-frame list at 0x0059D8E8: {obj, obj+0x34, obj+0x12C, +0x130, +0x134}, stride 5 dwords. Skipped when obj+0x34 bit 0x8000 is set, and taken only when bit 0x10 is set or obj+0x78 <= 0. It feeds two consumers, not one: the gunshot hit test, and -- after FUN_00405360 copies it to 0x005A30A0 -- ColiTestSphereAgainstActors, which is the actor-versus-actor push. So a class that never calls this takes no part in separating a crowd.
billboarded sprite-animation effect by kind
maps an effect kind to its asset slot range
obj+0x1390 is a PARENT ACTOR here, not a descriptor tail
alloc 0x13F4; reads desc+0x24/+0x25 inline; does NOT set obj+0x1390

obj+0x34 = the spawn record's flags word | 1, and obj+0x38 = 0. Run by SpawnFromDescriptor BEFORE the class's own Init, which then ORs its bits on top. This is where the descriptor's flags become the actor's: bit 15 takes it out of the shot test and the crowd push, bit 17 skips the per-frame ground snap in ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors so a spawn placed on a ledge stays on it (95 spawns), bit 18 tells EnemyZombieInit not to compute the aim angles, bit 27 picks between row[2] and row[3] (155 spawns), and bit 14 freezes the pose.
opcodes 0x0B/0x0D; alloc 0x13F4; obj+0x1390 = descriptor + 0x24
opcode 0x0C; alloc 0x1314; obj+0x130C = descriptor + 0x24
Takes the first free general slot, 2..13; slots 0 and 1 are reserved for enemies holding an attack permit. The slot index is kept in obj+0x120.
14-slot table at g_hit_slots; sets obj+0x38 |= 0x40
body-part and damage tables indexed by actor type
decrements obj+0x11C only
adds the difficulty delta to obj+0x11E, clamps [1,300], copies to obj+0x11C
fills the 112-slot array from the {class,handler} pairs
internally push/pop balanced

Start a motion on the track with a **cross-fade**: the fourth argument is the fade length in frames, stored at track+0x30 as length+1, alongside the start frame at +0x08 and its half at +0x18. Every class-0x30 state passes one -- 5 for ZombieStateApproach's walk and ZombieStateStrike's swing, 10 for the attack run, the hold's idle, ZombieStateBackOff's retreat, the lunge and ZombieStateWaitTurn. ActorSetMotion (FUN_00411930) is the one that does not fade, and it is used for the scripted cues that are meant to cut.
6-record ring of per-shot effects, per player
lit variant of AssetDrawSlot, same slot
id >> 28 selects the category table at 0x0041D324
a bare RET; the filler entry in every dispatch table
score -> rank 0..7; picks the ending track
identity function; descriptors are already relocated pointers

evt 0x46. The EvtOpWaitEnemiesPresent43 handler with g_civilians_alive (0x009CA0E8) in place of g_enemies_present: same DAT_009C8EA0 yield latch, same DAT_007DCCA4 gameplay-live gate, same DAT_009C6F2D side condition. All 68 sites in the shipped scripts pass operand 0, so in practice it waits for the last civilian to leave play.
sets COLORARG1=TEXTURE, COLORARG2=DIFFUSE, ALPHAARG1=TEXTURE
unlinks the actor and longjmps; does not return
ActorAlloc(entry_fn, size) stores entry_fn at obj[0]
ALPHABLENDENABLE = (tsp & 0x180000) != 0x80000
draws the opaque pass immediately, in submission order
sorts by (draw layer asc, sort depth desc) then draws the translucent pass
the qsort comparator behind the draw order
push(0) duplicates the top
wipes the top 3x3; a screen-axis billboard
reads the motion frame, sets the object root pose, then walks the node tree
per node: Translate(bone offset); RotZ; RotY; RotX from frame+0x0C+bone*6

Start a clip at frame zero with **no cross-fade**: writes the motion id to track+0x20, zeroes the frame counter (track+0x00), the play cursor (track+0x08), track+0x10 and track+0x18, and clears the two fade bytes at +0x36/+0x37, so nothing of the outgoing clip is left to blend from. ActorSetMotionBlended (FUN_004119A0) is the fading half of the pair; this one is for the scripted cues that are meant to cut, and ZombieStateMotionCue21 is one of them.
motion job sub-step 0: builds "mot\%s", CreateFileA, allocates size+0x20
sub-step 1: one ReadFile of the whole bank -- mot/ is NOT compressed
sub-step 2: the entire parse -- one int32 offset per motion id in the bank
asset job kind 8; dispatches the sub-step at job+0x0C
asset job kind 9
asset job kind 10
((bones*6+15)&~3)*frame + 4 + slot.base; bones from the CHARACTER type
enqueues asset job kind 8 for a bank id

column1: # --- combat: shots, damage, dismemberment, death; characters, motion, props ---

column3: walks g_pCharacterSkeletons[char_type] -- the SAME tree the renderer draws through
per bone: sphere, or mesh when record+0x88 != -1; recurses into children
ray vs the bone's hit sphere from g_pBoneHitSpheres, appended to g_ShotHitList
precise test against the bone's own collision mesh in its local space
origin -> origin + direction * 1000
the miss: ColiSegmentVsMesh against the full and ray-only collision sets
unprojects the crosshair with g_projection_distance_px (640.21) and writes the per-player shot record at g_ShotRecords
rotates the centre into the shot frame with the precomputed sin/cos and compares the perpendicular distance to the radius
picks which players resolve, randomising the order in two-player
per-bone, per-difficulty addend from g_pBoneDamageByRank
writes the effect slot into record[0] -- the slot the bone DRAWS -- so a hit replaces that body part
gives the swapped part its own hit sphere from the TAIL of g_pBoneHitSpheres, past bone_count-1 entries, terminated by slot == -1
draws record[bone].slot; record base obj+0x20C, stride 0x90
class 0x33, switch on obj+0x11C
class 0x33 selector 2: draws params[0] until params[3] == cam frame or g_script_flags[params.u8(0x11)]. The stage-2 van bodies are these
installs CheckCutsceneSkipRequest from the task table at 0x005934E4
THE link that makes the skip work: raises g_nEvtSkipFlag when Start was pressed inside a skippable region; also ends the current camera move (cam_end = cam_frame) and drains the asset queue
clears DAT_009A2230 one frame later and ends the task
class 0x30. params[0] = character type, params[2] = initial state (obj+0x1310), obj+0x1B4 = motion 0x3BC (956, zom.bin) or 0x41E on a branch
per frame: dispatches g_pZombieStates[obj+0x1310], then integrates velocity

Class 0x30 state 6. sub 0 chooses the death motion; sub 1 raises obj+0x34 bits 0x22000, sets obj+0x136C 0x60000000, plays the death voice (FUN_00456600, which also counts down DAT_009C8A74) and runs ZombieReleasePermitAndUntrack (FUN_004565A0) -- so the permit and the commit latch are freed on death, by the state machine, not by the shot. sub 2 waits for the clip: at g_motion_play_length - 1 it hands to FUN_00456740, or to state 12 when obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 is set.
special deaths for a destroyed part (obj+0x1368 bits -> 428/421/633/553), else falls through to the directional pick
camera_yaw - actor_yaw against four +/-45 degree arcs: 0x4000 -> 992, 0xC000 -> 991, 0x0000 -> g_pDeathMotionsArc0[4], 0x8000 -> g_pDeathMotionsArc8000[6]

Class 0x30 state 21, the entrance that arrives on a clip -- the stage-2 van zombies and four more in stage 5, all six playing motion 923. sub 0 sets the descriptor's clip (params+0x04) with ActorSetMotion, no fade, and arms params+0x08 frames at obj+0x1330; it falls straight into sub 1, which counts that down and then **clears obj+0x34 bit 0x4000**; sub 2 plays the clip out. This state is the ONLY thing in the game that clears the three bits the spawn record sets to park the actor inside the vehicle: 0x4000 when the delay expires, 0x100 at obj+0x19C == 0x26 of clip 0x39B (the landing, so it stops ricocheting), and 0x2000 as it hands over. Exit is g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1 <= obj+0x19C -- the play clock, not the authored frame count -- to descriptor byte 3, substituting state 1 if that byte names 21 again; on the byte-3 == 4 arm it inlines TestApproachRing to seed obj+0x1358 first, an arm no shipped record takes. Skipping this state leaves the freeze bit on for ever: ZombieAdvanceMotion then never advances obj+0x194/0x198, and since a zombie is carried only by its clip's root motion it can never close either.
opens with if (g_nEvtSkipFlag == 0) -- the gate is real, not dead
as 0x3A, 0x10-byte operand
class 0x44, indexes the 18 builders at g_pPropBuilders
selector 1, 37 spawns: one hinge from the parameter tail
selector 2: two doors at literal offsets (+/-9.29, 11.5, 22.68), slots 0x1794/0x1795, half a turn apart
selector 4, 13 spawns: as selector 1 with a per-instance scale and the flags at different offsets
shared by class 0x44 selectors 1/2/4. Swings on g_script_flags[open_flag] through g_pHingeCurvesXYZ / g_pHingeCurvesYaw; transform is RotY(base); RotZ(rz); RotY(swing); RotX(rx)
Search g_character_skeletons[char_type] for the node whose bone index (+0x14) is the argument. Starts at the root's children, so the root itself is never returned.
Recursive half of FindSkeletonNodeForBone. Node layout: +0x14 u16 bone, +0x16 u16 child count, +0x18 child pointers.

Run when a bone reaches its sever step (effect-table next == 1, or a torso hit that kills). Calls RemoveBoneSubtree on every CHILD of that bone -- the bone itself keeps the stump model ActorSwapDamagedPart just gave it, and everything below it disappears.

Sets the destroyed-zone bit in obj+0x1318, zeroes the bone's draw slot (rec+0x00) and rec+0x78, then recurses into its children. A zero draw slot is both invisible and unshootable: ShotTestBoneTree tests `if (rec[0] != 0)`.
Returns g_damage_rank, the 0..15 adaptive rank DamageRankModifier indexes. NOT g_difficulty.
Seeds g_damage_rank from g_initial_damage_rank[difficulty] when a game starts; forces difficulty 2 when FUN_00413280 is nonzero.
Adaptive difficulty. Re-derives g_damage_rank from lives lost since the last update and elapsed time (0x708 ticks per step), clamped to [0,15].
Start a motion on one of the actor's two motion tracks; the track index is the last argument (0 the looping motion, 1 the one-shot the hit reaction uses).
MotionCrossFadeTo with a different flag pair (block+0x38 |= 9); used by the alternate hit reaction indexed by the last-hit zone.
Start a motion on track 1 cross-fading from what is playing. block+0x33 = fade + 1 -- ActorPlayHitReaction passes 20 when the hit severed something and 10 otherwise.
The blood flipbook: AssetDrawSlot(frame + 0x3A) for 25 frames at the hit bone, in view space, scaled (-view_z*0.0375 + 0.25) * 0.3 * severity.
Spawn the blood flipbook at a bone. Arg 3 is the severity scale ActorShotFeedback picks: 0.5 damaged, 0.75 damaged and swapped, 1.0 severed.
Collision material -> ricochet sound. The filenames it resolves to are what name the materials: 1 sand, 2 metal, 3 other, 5 water, 6 wood.
A shot that hit the world: takes the surface material from the collision hit record (+0x30) and spawns the matching sprite and sound.
Two sounds per event: a flesh impact from DAT_00577674[0..4] and a voice from one of two sets, chosen by character type. Kind 0 hurt, 1 killed, 2 headshot kill.
The zombie's shot reaction: DispatchHit, then per player ActorShotFeedback and either ActorReactToHit (alive) or the death voice and state 6 (dead).
Draws the hit: blood at the bone scaled by g_hit_result, or -- on result 5 -- an impact sprite and a metal ricochet, because the shot did nothing.
Derives obj+0x130C, the body condition, from which parts are gone. Both arm zones destroyed (obj+0x1318 bits 1 and 2) gives condition 5, which ChooseDeathMotion reads.
Records the last-hit zone in obj+0x1319 (1 torso, 2 head) and decides whether the hit interrupts what the actor is doing. Results 1 and 3 always react; 2 and 5 only for character types 3 and 0x12.
The stumble. g_pHitReactionMotions[char][obj+0x130C][g_bone_reaction_group[bone]] cross-faded onto track 1 -- or hard-set with no fade when the bone is 9 or above, the pelvis and legs.

The advance. Sub-state 0 measures the actor's distance to the CAMERA (not to a player) and picks a step count from which of g_enemy_approach_rings' three radii it falls inside; sub-state 1 walks that many steps and then hands to the state named by the descriptor tail's byte 3.
Installs CameraFollowPlayerMidpoint as the camera update hook, plus the per-player draw helper. One of eight installers that write g_camera_update_hook.
Installs CameraStepDeferredRailWithFrameExport as the camera update hook.

Per frame: evaluates the active cam/ path's look-at into g_camera_lookat_target, then eases the camera block's current target (block+0xD8) toward it. The easing is why the pan is smooth rather than a snap.

Picks what the camera looks at. Walks g_enemy_slots; an enemy holding an attack permit (obj+0x121 != -1) is focused ALONE, otherwise the midpoint of two registered enemies is used, and with no enemies registered it falls back to the cam/ path's own target channel. This is the gameplay tracking camera.

Angle between the camera's current look direction and the desired one, clamped to 0x1FFF (45 deg) and used to index PTR_DAT_00576C04 -- the turn-rate curve, so a bigger swing turns at a different rate.

Steady-state body of CameraSnapToPathEye, reached by that function re-pointing g_camera_update_hook at itself+N. Writes only the eye, never the angles -- which is how the camera holds position while SelectCameraLookAtTarget swings the look-at.

Steady-state body of CameraStepDeferredRailWithFrameExport. Advances the stashed path frame, evaluates eye and target as independent channels, takes yaw from (eye - target) and forces pitch and roll to zero.
Clears g_enemy_slots, the 16-entry {u8 occupied; void *actor} table the tracking camera reads.
Frees this actor's camera slot: g_enemy_slots[obj+0x120] = 0, obj+0x120 = 0xFF.

An approaching enemy asks permission to attack. One permit per player in g_attack_permits, count from g_max_attackers; on success it stores the permit index in obj+0x121 and returns 1, which is what lets ZombieStateApproach hand over to the attack state -- and what makes the camera focus on that enemy.
Frees the attack permit at obj+0x121 and clears the global commit latch.
Decrements g_enemies_alive exactly once, guarded by obj+0x38 bit 1. This is what opens wait_enemies_alive.
Decrements g_enemies_present exactly once, guarded by obj+0x38 bit 2. This is what opens wait_enemies_present, and it is separate from the alive count.
Camera tick that eases the look-at onto the path's own target, then locks: once the dot product of desired and current exceeds 0.99999 it flips to evaluating the path straight into the camera block.

Camera mode 2's sub-handler 1. NOT what the old name CameraStartTurnOntoPathTarget claimed: the bytes at 0x00402867 are C6 05 2D 6F 9C 00 01, which writes g_camera_free = 1 -- the *path* branch -- along with 0x009C6F2C = 0. It abandons the turn after one damped step and hands the camera back to the path. It is also unreachable: its only reference is entry 1 of the sub-table at 0x00576CE0, selected by byte 0x009C6F2E, whose sole writer (0x0040322D) stores 0.

The gameplay camera. Calls SelectCameraLookAtTarget, eases the block's look-at onto the result with TurnLookAtToward, and takes the turn rate from ComputeLookAtAngleError while enemies are registered or a flat constant when none are.
Eases the camera block's eye toward the path's eye channel at 1/16 per frame, leaving the look-at to the tracking code.
Rotates a look-at point toward a desired one by num/(num+rate) of the angle between them and re-emits it at a fixed 100-unit radius from the eye. Rate 0 snaps; larger is slower.
Loads the stashed path id and frame for the current branch variable and evaluates it into the camera block.
Rebuilds g_enemy_slots each frame from the radix-sorted candidate list: enemies holding an attack permit take slots 0 and 1, everyone else fills from slot 2.

Adds an actor to the camera candidate list unless obj+0x34 bit 0x10000 is set -- which ZombieStateApproach sets while walking and clears when the actor wins an attack permit, so only committed enemies are ever tracked. Key is (int)(|actor - camera eye| * 10.0).
LSD radix sort, two 8-bit passes, over the {distance key, actor} candidate list -- nearest first.
Eases the actor's yaw (obj+0x68) toward a point 1.5 units in front of the camera.
Returns which advance ring the actor is in -- 1 inside the inner radius (strike range), 2, 3, 4 outward -- and sets obj+0x1358 to the step count that band allows.
Class-0x30 state 1. Plays the run motion, closes on the camera, and switches to state 2 when TestApproachRing returns 1.

Class-0x30 state 15, the commonest scripted entrance after the attack run: 50 spawns across the game. sub 0 latches obj+0x1370 from the FLOAT at descriptor tail +0x04 and falls through into sub 1, which records the start point at obj+0x13C0/C4/C8 and parks sub at 2. Every frame after that it plays row[2 + ((obj+0x34 >> 0x1B) & 1)] from a random start frame -- row[4] instead when obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 is set -- and writes the 2D distance from the start point to obj+0x1374. Reaching obj+0x1370 records obj+0x13D8/DC/E0 and hands to state 1, or to ZombieReleaseAndDespawn on the 0x20000000 arm. It never moves the actor: SkeletonApplyRootMotion does, out of the clip. There is no destination and no route -- class 0x30 has no path-following state at all (PATH_STATES is class 0x31 only), so everything past tail+0x08 belongs to the next descriptor, not to this one.
Per-frame root pose: reads the current motion frame, or blends two of them by DAT_007C1C24 when the cross-fade flag is set (obj+0x37 & 0x21), and applies the root translation and rotation.

Converts the frame-to-frame delta of the motion root into world movement when obj+0x64 bit 1 is set, rotating it by the actor's own orientation, then calls the per-frame pose hook at motion block +0x115C.
The default per-frame pose hook: does nothing. Every skeletal actor installed by FUN_00410440 gets this one.

The only other per-frame pose hook in the program. Ramps the actor's radius (obj+0x128) toward a target and pushes it out of world collision along the hit normal. It does NOT rotate any bone -- see the note on upper-body aim in docs/formats/combat.md.

Class-0x30 state 2. Holds inside the inner ring, plays the in-range idle and its sound, and on the attack cooldown asks TryClaimAttackSlot again -- success moves to state 3, the strike. Drops back to state 4 if the actor has drifted outside the inner ring.

Class-0x30 state 3. Sub 0 draws an attack from g_class30_attack_picks by (rand%10 + destroyed_zones*10); sub 1 plays the lunge until inside the attack's own distance then starts the strike and shouts (ActorPlayHitVoice kind 3); sub 2 runs the clip and calls ActorStrikeConnect on the exact frame the entry names.
Lands the strike on the player named by the attack permit (obj+0x121). Whiffs when every zone in the entry's cancel mask has been shot off -- so blowing an arm off stops the attack that swings it.

One life, -100 points, 0x5A frames of invulnerability, and _DAT_009A3794 -= 2, which UpdateDamageRank consumes -- being hit lowers the adaptive rank and makes the game easier. There is no variable damage against the player.
PlayerTakeDamage with an explicit invulnerability duration and an override that ignores the current one.
Rejects a player index that is not 0 or 1, and rejects a hit while the player entity is in a state other than 1 or 4..5 during app state 6.
Called when an attack is interrupted: releases the slots, sets body condition 4 and hands the actor to its leave state.

Once a frame: sorts the registration list by distance to the camera and writes **two** different ranks. Pass one: obj+0x131D gets the raw distance rank, nearest first, and obj+0x131E is set to 0xE. Then entries that are not live, or that carry obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 -- which ZombieStateBackOff sets while it retreats -- are dropped, and pass two numbers the survivors 0, 1, 2 into obj+0x131E. So the compacted rank is the queue with the retreating actors taken out, and it is what the '< 3' cap tests, while the ring allowance tests the raw one. The list holds fourteen; a fifteenth enemy is never ranked and keeps 0xFF, which reads as -1 and passes every test.

A radix sort over the distance-rank registration list: two 8-bit passes on the u16 key at DAT_005A4D58, moving the {key, actor} pairs through the scratch at DAT_005A4E38 and back. Called by RankEnemiesByDistance and nothing else; it only orders, it does not move anyone.
Adds a live, not-yet-dead actor to the distance-ranked enemy list, at most 14.
Derives obj+0x130C from whether bones 5 and 8 -- the hands, at obj+0x4DC and obj+0x68C, which are 0x20C + bone*0x90 -- still hold their original draw slots, and sets the matching destroyed-zone bits.
TurnActorTowardCamera without the 1.5-unit forward offset: eases the actor's yaw toward the camera eye itself.
Class 0x15. Spawns N copies of a prop spaced by a delta vector; each samples the wave field for its height.

One travelling source's contribution. phase = (|cos yaw| > 0.5 ? cos(yaw)*p.z : sin(yaw)*p.x) + src.phase; height = cos(2*pi*phase/wavelength) * amplitude. The 65536 scale and the BAMS cosine make it a plain sinusoid truncated to BAMS resolution. FPU args are dropped by the decompiler -- read from the disassembly.
One circular source's contribution. r = hypot(p.x-src.x, p.z-src.z); height = cos(2*pi*r/wavelength) * amplitude * max(0, 1 - r*0.01), so a ripple dies at 100 units.

Class 0x16. Allocates the 0x2C-byte wave-field manager and records the water plane Y from the spawn descriptor's y -- the descriptor's x and z are ignored, so the field is a global plane height, not a placed object.
Reads {amplitude, wavelength, speed} from the descriptor tail on its first tick, installs WaveEvalTravelling, then advances the source's phase by speed every frame.
Same setup with WaveEvalCircular, then walks the source itself along its BAMS yaw at speed -- x += sin(yaw)*speed, z += cos(yaw)*speed.
Class 0x17. Claims one of eight source slots, copies the spawn position and its three orientation words into it, and picks travelling or circular from g_wave_source_kinds by obj+0x11C.
Sums every active source's contribution at a point. This is a height QUERY for floating objects -- the water surface itself is static level geometry and is never displaced by it.

Class 0x31, subtypes 0x16-0x19. Subtype 0x16 is zsass.bin and puts asset slots 0x1FA2 and 0x1F9E into bone 5 and bone 8's draw slots (obj+0x4DC / obj+0x68C) -- the hands, holding an item, in place of the bare-hand parts 0x1F9F and 0x1F9B. Stage 2 block 5 spawns two of them at y=87 with 130 hit points, out of walking reach, so the item is thrown. Its own state machine is at LAB_00449910 and is [open].

Per-class hook called as a strike begins. In body condition 6 -- wading -- it queries the ground under the actor and, if g_coli_hit_surface is 5 or 0x37, plays a splash and spawns sprite material 0x61 (0x62 in state 0x17). The same two surface ids as coli.py's WET_SURFACES.
The per-frame half of the same hook: one splash 0x14 frames before the clip ends, latched by obj+0x136C bit 0x10000.

Class-0x31 state 29. Plays motion 5 and at the clip's midpoint puts the weapon back in whichever hand is bare -- restoring the draw slot, its hit sphere at rec+0x78, and clearing that arm's destroyed-zone bit.

Takes an attack permit, picks a hand with FUN_0044F630, reads its entry from g_class31_throws[body_condition], plays the throw clip and calls SpawnThrownWeapon on the frame the entry names. Then hands to state 7.

Allocates the projectile at the throwing hand's bone position, sets its model from the character type, leaves the hand bare, marks that arm's destroyed zone, and passes the thrower's attack permit to the weapon -- so the projectile damages the player the thrower had claimed.
Sets the weapon's target to a point 4 units in front of the camera, offset sideways by 0.6 per player in two-player.

Projectile state 0. Launch sets ttl = distance * 0.8333 and velocity = (target - pos)/ttl, so the flight is a straight line at a constant speed. Every flight frame it tumbles the weapon by adding obj+0x135C to **obj+0x68** -- the Y term of ThrownWeaponUpdate's Rz*Ry*Rx draw, so the spin is about the weapon's own vertical -- negated unless obj+0x1358 is 5, which is which hand threw it. On ttl expiry it calls PlayerTakeDamage outright: the hit is TIMED, not tested. Then AimThrownWeapon points it back at the camera, it sticks for 0x1E frames and blinks for 0x3C by toggling obj+0x1F8 bit 0.
Projectile state 1, entered when the weapon is shot out of the air. Spawns an impact sprite, plays BULLET_MET3, picks a random direction and flies off before despawning.

The projectile's own update: two states at 0x00592AE0, then draws its model as Rz(obj+0x6C) * Ry(obj+0x68) * Rx(obj+0x1364 + obj+0x64). The **Y** term is the tumble -- ThrownWeaponFlyToTarget accumulates it into obj+0x68 -- and the X and Z terms are zero in flight, set only when the weapon lands and turns to face the camera. Registers for both the shot test and camera tracking, so a thrown weapon can be shot down and the camera will follow it.
Class-0x31 update: a cooldown, a pre-hook, dispatch through g_class31_states, then velocity += acceleration and position += velocity -- this class integrates ballistically, unlike class 0x30.

Class-0x30 state 4, entered after a strike. Plays the back-away walk from g_class30_motion_rows[cond][4], turns away from the position recorded when the strike began, and KEEPS the attack permit until the actor is back outside the inner approach ring or 240 frames have passed -- only then does it release and hand to state 2. That retreat is the pause between attacks; there is no cooldown timer for an ordinary zombie.
Eases the actor's yaw toward the direction (actor - point), the mirror of TurnActorTowardCamera. ZombieStateBackOff passes the position the strike started from.

Step an angle toward another by at most *rate* BAMS per frame -- a rate limit, not an ease. ZombieStateHoldAtRange and ZombieStateWaitTurn pass 0x40 and ZombieStateBackOff -0x40, which is a third of a degree a frame: slow enough that a retreating actor cannot whip round when it passes the point it is turning relative to.

Class 0x31's copy of TryClaimAttackSlot, instruction for instruction. Neither tests the distance queue -- that gate lives in ZombieStateApproach, before the call -- so a thrower may claim from any range.

Class 0x30: snap the yaw at obj+0x68 straight to the player and record that player's position in obj+0x13E4/E8/EC. With one attacker the target is the camera eye; with two it is a point (+/-1.2, 0, -1.5) in front of the camera per permit index, so the two zombies converge on different shoulders. ZombieStateStrike measures its lunge distance against the recorded point, not against the camera.

Class 0x30 state 24. Sub 0 reads a destination (float x,y,z at descriptor +0x04/08/0C) and a frame count (s16 at +0x10) and sets obj+0x4C velocity = (dest - pos)/frames, which EnemyZombieUpdate then integrates -- a scripted leap or drop, not gravity. On arrival it parks the position in obj+0x13C0..C8, claims a permit, plays the clip at descriptor +0x18 and calls PlayerTakeDamage on the frame at descriptor +0x1C.

Class 0x31 state 2, the knockdown and the death fall. Sub 0 clears the surface bits, plays g_class31_motion_sets[set][5] -- the airborne clip, 0x3A6 / 0x3A4 / 0x1BC / 0x3A6 by set -- blended on a first entry and hard-rewound on a re-entry (obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, which also counts obj+0x1328 up), and launches ThrowerBeginKnockbackArc while obj+0x1328 is at most 1. Sub 1 rides the arc, freezing the pose at frame 35/20/44/44 by character type, then sets obj+0x5C = -0.05444444. Sub 2 falls until QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+4.5, z) catches it or obj+0x1338 reaches 0x78, snaps, records the surface in obj+0x1350, bounces with vel.y *= -0.5 and vel.xz *= 0.5, plays effect 0x46 and sound 0x2716A9, and re-bounces while the vertical speed is over 0.15 -- character type 0x16 never re-bounces. Sub 3 splits: alive and not on surface 0x5A, it lies still for (rand()%10+1)*3 frames, plays 0x11B unless it is character 0x17 and gets up through sub 4 into state 0x11 when obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 is set or ThrowerPickNextState otherwise; dead, or on surface 0x5A, it waits for obj+0x1F1 -- the motion block's clip-ran-out flag -- and goes to state 3 for character 0x16 or ThrowerEnterCorpseState for the rest, spawning effect 0x61 on a 0x5A landing in scene 3 block 4.

Class 0x31's per-frame shot drain, run before the state dispatch. Calls DispatchHit -- which is where ResolveHit actually applies the damage -- then walks g_hit_player_order (0x009C8908; it is NOT g_hit_slots), writes the bone index to obj+0x1368, and runs ThrowerShotFeedback. Unless obj+0x34 bit 0x100, hit result 5, or obj+0x136C bit 0x200000 already latched, it releases the attack permit and picks the reaction: on the killing blow state 2 with voice kind 2 for bone 2 else 1; alive and obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 clear, state 0x21 for character type 0x18, state 1 when already in state 7 and on the ground, otherwise state 2 -- and obj+0x136C bit 0x400000 latches a re-entry when a reaction was already running. It never writes obj+0x1364, which is where ZombieOnShot puts the hit result.

Class 0x30's post-state motion step: draws the skinned model and then advances the motion frame counters at obj+0x194 and obj+0x198. Gated off by obj+0x34 bit 0x4000, which is how a state freezes a pose -- the gate is on the counters only, so the model is still drawn, but root motion is a frame-to-frame delta and a frozen counter therefore also stops the actor moving. ZombieStateMotionCue21 is the only thing that clears the bit for a spawn record that sets it. In g_GameMode 2 the advance additionally needs DAT_009c72f1 == 1 and DAT_009c72f3 == 0, and swaps the hook at obj+0x12EC between FUN_004534A0 and LAB_00453B30.
Class 0x31's copy of ZombieAdvanceMotion.

Start a motion unless obj+0x136C bit 0x2000 holds the current one, the motion is already playing, or bit 0x1000 asks for the track to be stopped instead. The states call this rather than ActorSetMotion so a reaction in progress is not cut off.

Picks the ground-shadow ellipse size by character type -- 50x30 for types 0x44 and 0x47, 11x10 for everything else -- and calls ActorDrawGroundShadow. Skipped when obj+0x34 bit 0x80000 is set or obj+0x1F8 bit 0 is clear.

Draws asset slot 0x10D0 as a flattened ellipse on the ground under the actor. The height comes from QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+3, z) when obj+0x1F8 bit 2 is set, from obj+0x44 otherwise, and from g_camera_fixed_eye_y while g_app_state is 0x0D.

Runs every class-0x30 frame unless obj+0x1368 bit 1 is already set. Queries the ground at y+20 and, if the surface underneath is 5 or 0x37 -- the two WET_SURFACES -- and the actor has fallen below it, calls FUN_00408740 to put it in the water and latches bit 1 so it only happens once.

The body of DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow: parks the track and bone records in g_motion_track/g_motion_bone_records, walks g_character_skeletons[type] emitting each node, then runs the actor's attachment list.

Class 0x31 state 20, and how a spawn placed in the air reaches the ground. Sub 0 hands the actor's position and the descriptor's destination (float x,y,z at +0x04/08/0C) and duration (s32 at +0x10) to ActorArcBegin; each frame ActorArcStep integrates the arc, and when it ends the actor drops into state 7 to stand and throw. Stage 2 block 5 spawns two zsass at y = 87 whose descriptors name the street at y = 37, 50 units down over 30 and 35 frames.

Record a ballistic arc: source in obj+0x13C0/C4/C8, destination in obj+0x13CC/D0/D4, duration in obj+0x1334, frame counter obj+0x1330 reset. ActorArcVelocity then rebuilds the velocity every frame from those.
Advance one frame of an arc begun by ActorArcBegin. Returns 0 once the frame counter passes the duration, which is how the leap states know they have landed.

The arc itself, and it is exact projectile motion: vel.xz = (dst - src)/T flat, and vel.y = -0.027222222*n + (T*T*0.027222222 + 2*dy)/(2*T) for frame n of T. The 0.027222222 is half the 0.05444444 gravity ThrowerStateFallAndLand uses, which is what a discrete `pos += vel; vel -= g` integrator needs. The six cases select which axis carries the arc.

Class 0x30 state 5, and the way back into the attack loop. Plays the in-place walk from the motion row, turns to the camera at 0x40 a frame, and returns to state 1 the moment `(s8)obj+0x131D < obj+0x1358` -- its rank in the distance queue is inside the allowance again. ZombieStateAttackRun sends an actor here when it drops out of that slice, so the queue throttle is a round trip and not a one-way exit. Note the **signed** read: EnemyZombieInit writes 0xFF to obj+0x131D, which is -1, so an actor that has not been ranked yet passes the test rather than failing it.

Begin an arc from the actor's position to a named point. Records src in obj+0x13C0..C8 and dst in obj+0x13CC..D4, zeroes the frame counter, and sets the duration at obj+0x1334 to n - n%step where n = (int)(dist2d * step) -- the **2D** distance, x and z only, y is not in it. So step is frames per unit: 1 gives a unit a frame, 2 gives half. The same value is passed to ActorArcStep as the arc kind, so it selects which axis carries the arc as well as the speed. Ghidra drops the FPU argument to __ftol here and shows the distance as nothing at all.

Begin the leg of a path: ActorArcBeginTo to the waypoint's destination, then install the waypoint's motion set. Character type 0x19 uses a different arc builder. When the set is the default it instead draws an attack index from g_class31_picks the way ZombieStateStrike does, so a waypoint can arrive swinging.

Class 0x31 state 26: follow a predefined path. Sub 0 reads a delay from descriptor +0x04 and points obj+0x1394 at the waypoint list, which starts at descriptor +0x08 and runs in **16-byte entries** -- {s16 step, s16 motion_set, f32 x, f32 y, f32 z} -- terminated by a step of -1. Sub 1 counts the delay down; sub 2 begins the leg with ActorArcBeginToWaypoint; sub 3 steps the arc and, on arrival, plays sound 0x2916A9 and advances the cursor. At the terminator, character type 0x17 goes to state 7 and everything else claims an attack permit and goes to state 9.

Class 0x41's handler. A transient stub: dispatches obj+0x130C through the 79-entry g_class41_constructors, then falls into ActorKill so the placer never survives its first frame. It is never drawn and never damaged -- what the script places is the constructor call, not an object.

g_class41_constructors[0]. Builds one BreakablePropUpdate child per member of breakable group obj+0x11C, from the 10-byte records at g_breakable_group_ptrs. x/z are the record's s16 tenths; y is g_camera_fixed_eye_y - 0.1 + level*7.540296, except group 7 which uses level*7.540296 - 14.9 off its own pointer. Each child gets +0x11C = 2 (two shots), asset 0x19E8, the placer's evt-block lifetime in +0x199, and its member index in +0x290. In g_GameMode 2 the members g_prop_target_set selects get +0x11C = 1 and asset 0x1A0F instead. Finally it seeds g_item_set_countdown for the group's item set with rand()%n + 1 -- so the hidden item drops on a RANDOM one of that set's props, not the last.

g_class41_constructors[4], the most-placed type (70 spawns). Builds one prop with update FUN_00465fb0 from the *orientation* words: obj+0x6C is the object kind and obj+0x64 the item-set size, which is why the class-0x41 orientation triple must never be read as angles. The kind indexes g_prop_kind_params (stride 0xC) for the break effect and radius, and picks the asset slot: 2 -> 0x17A9, 3 -> 0x19E8, 8 -> 0x17AA, 9 -> 0x17AB, else none.

The breakable prop placed by PlaceBreakableGroup. Despawns once g_evt_step_index has changed more than its +0x199 lifetime times -- a lifetime in event STEPS, not blocks. On a shot: +0x11C 2 -> 1 cracks it, plays 0x1D16A9 and sets +0x2C0 = 1.0 so it shakes, and marks every member it supports to shake too; +0x11C 1 -> 0 destroys it, plays 0x1A16A9, awards through BreakablePropAwardHit, clears its slot in g_breakable_members and decrements g_item_set_countdown -- releasing the set's item when that reaches zero. Destroying and toppling are DIFFERENT: a destroyed prop at stack level 0 has its object entry point overwritten with BreakableEffectUpdate and becomes a puff for 0x48 frames, and one above level 0 shatters through BreakablePropSpawnShatter -- neither falls. Falling (state 1 -> 2, settled by BreakablePropGroundContact) happens only to a prop whose supporting members have all gone, which is what makes a stack collapse from the bottom. Note also that only the destroying shot pays: the crack calls BreakablePropAwardHit with award=0.

Transforms the 96 points of g_breakable_hull_points by the prop's Ry*Rz*Rx and reports whether any of them is below the floor (g_camera_fixed_eye_y - 0.1). In the falling state it records the first such point in +0x198; in the toppling state it keeps the lowest and re-seats the prop's origin on it, which is how a broken prop comes to rest leaning on a corner. Also clamps z into [-1325, -1265.8] while g_scene is 1.

Resolves which player's shot landed from obj+0x34 bits 1 and 2 -- both set means rand() picks -- then awards 10 points unless the caller passes 0 or g_GameMode is 2, and counts the hit into g_player_hit_count for the accuracy grade.

Breaks a stacked prop into 15 fragments: allocates a 0x2B4 object running FUN_004653b0 and seeds each fragment from g_shatter_fragment_offsets and g_shatter_fragment_angles, with a radial velocity of 0.1..0.3 about the fragment's own bearing and a random spin of +/-0x400 on each axis.
The break puff. Draws the effect record at +0x324 for 0x48 frames and then kills itself.
The impact spark on a prop hit. Allocates a 0x50 object with effect id 0x904 at the shot's screen point unprojected to the prop's depth.
+1 to g_player_lives, or 300 points instead when the player is already at the cap -- g_max_lives, or the per-player Boss Mode cap at 0x009A2245 + p*0x14.
Releases item-set 1: a 0x378 object running ExtraLifePickupUpdate, one unit above the prop, turned to face the camera.

The extra-life pickup, drawn as asset 0x10C3. When shot it calls GrantExtraLife for the player who hit it, plays 0x3616A9, swaps to the floating award sprite (0x116A/0x119C with 0x1256/0x1257 above it) and fades out over 0x31 frames. BreakablePropAwardHit is called with 0 here, so the pickup itself pays no 10 points.

Releases item-set 3: a full 0x13F4 actor of character type 0x1C, whose skeleton slots all resolve to frog_gold.bin -- the golden frog. It is placed at the prop, turned to face the camera, and runs FUN_00471fa0 with FUN_00463f90 installed at +0x12EC.

Releases item-sets 2 and 5..8: a 0x378 object running ScorePickupUpdate with the set id as its kind, at the prop's position raised by g_item_pickup_y_offset[kind] and drawn with g_item_pickup_slot[kind].

The g_GameMode == 1 release -- original/story per the g_GameMode row -- taken when the prop's +0x2A0 is not -1. Builds a 0x378 object running FUN_004675a0 with +0x2A0 as its kind. Three shipped members carry one: group 0 member 0 has kind 2 and group 7 members 3 and 4 have kind 5, and all three also hide an ordinary item set, so mode 1 substitutes its own drop for theirs.

The generic score pickup. On being shot it plays 0x416A9 or 0x3B17A9, awards g_item_score_table[kind], swaps to a floating score sprite (0x116A/0x119C), fades over 0x31 frames and despawns. Drawn as g_item_pickup_slot[kind] with a ground shadow at slot 0x10D0.

Class 0x31 state 9: off the roof and into shot. ThrowerStatePathFollow hands here for every character type but 0x17, having claimed an attack permit first. Sub 0 picks a landing point with ThrowerPickLandingPoint, faces g_camera_yaw_bams and begins an arc to it with step 1; the arc is stepped, the actor is re-snapped to the point each frame outside Training Mode, and at the end of the clip it goes to state 10.

Where a thrower lands, and it is a place on the **screen** rather than in the world: a pixel offset divided by g_projection_distance_px and unprojected at a fixed depth, so the actor always arrives the same distance in front of the camera however the camera is pointing. Depth -15.5 (-6.0 from state 0x17); vertical offset 390px for character type 0x16, 320 otherwise, and -350 from states 0x16/0x17. Sideways is +/-160px by attack permit and zero when g_max_attackers is 1.

Emits one node of the skeleton and, when its bone index matches the tracked one, records that node's **world position** into obj+0x100/104/108 -- which is what SelectCameraLookAtTarget aims the camera at, never obj+0x40. The bone is 1 for an ordinary humanoid (character types 0..0x14), 2 when obj+0x136C bit 0x10000000 is set, and 9 for body condition 5 or the g_camera_block_target case; obj+0x10C..114 gets the same point in the other space. A further -3.5 is applied to the height in the two-player attacker case. Recurses into the node's children.

Transforms obj+0x100 into view space for the shot test, runs RegisterForShotTest, then **raises obj+0x104 by its float argument** -- 4.0 for a class-0x30 zombie, 0 for a class-0x31 thrower -- and registers the actor for camera tracking. So the point the camera follows is the tracked bone lifted by four.

Projects the actor's tracked view-space point at obj+0x70/74/78 by g_projection_distance_px and asks whether it lands inside the frame -- half-width g_projection_distance_px * 0.5, half-height a literal 240. TryClaimAttackSlot calls it before handing out a permit, so an enemy off the side of the screen cannot start an attack, nor sit on the one permit while it is out of shot.

Rebuilds the actor's body sphere each frame: centre (x, y + obj+0x128 + 1, z) into obj+0x12C/130/134, with obj+0x124 -- g_actor_radius_by_char -- as the radius. The +1 becomes +0.5 when obj+0x136C bit 0x2000000 is set. Read by the shot test and the frustum test at FUN_0045CA60; **not** by anything that separates actors from each other.

The prop PlaceKindedProp builds -- class 0x41 type 4, 70 spawns and the most-placed constructor in the game. Shot handling depends on the model: a 0x19E8 crate takes two (the first cracks it, pays nothing and hides the model behind 0xFFFF), every other kind takes one. The destroying shot pays 10 through BreakablePropAwardHit, plays g_prop_kind_params[kind]+4, runs the break effect at +0x324 for DAT_004E07D0[effect]-2 frames and then despawns -- and releases the item set in +0x194 through the SAME g_item_set_countdown and the same switch BreakablePropUpdate uses. 37 of the 70 hide an item, which is more than the group placer accounts for. Draw-time shake, ground shadow 0x10D0 or 0x10D1 by kind.

The container PlaceFallingContainer builds -- class 0x44 selector 16. Two shots: the first pays nothing, swaps to slot 0xA51, plays 0xE16A9 and knocks it loose with an upward 0.8..1.09 and gravity 0.05444, so it tumbles and settles against the 48-point hull at 0x00594788; the second pays 10, plays 0x1716A9 or 0x1616A9, throws three FUN_0046AD20 fragments and releases its item set. Same g_item_set_countdown and the same release switch as class 0x41, so the two classes share one countdown per set. Lifetime is in evt blocks like the rest.
g_class44_subtypes[16]. Allocates a 0x378 object running FallingContainerUpdate. Two spawns, both stage 2.

g_class41_constructors[5..14, 18..21, 25, 27, 28, 30..36, 41, 43, 45, 49, 51, 53, 54, 56..60, 62..64, 67, 69..77] -- 44 of the 79 types and 173 of the class's 316 spawns. Allocates a 0x378 object whose update routine comes from the SECOND 79-entry table, g_class41_entries at 0x005936BC, which is how one constructor serves thirty different objects. The prologue copies the position, all three orientation words as real angles, and -- the trap -- obj+0x11C into obj+0x28C, so for this family the hp word is the ASSET SLOT. Then a switch on the type applies that object's own setup: a slot override (6, 10, 0x0D, 0x13, 0x38), a hit radius, a shot count, an effect id, or a whole sub-object list (8, 0x43, 0x2B). Case 0x22 builds a falling container -- the same object class 0x44 selector 16 places, item countdown and all. Cases 0x13 and 0x19 increment g_enemies_present and 0x0E g_enemies_alive, so some of what this places is not a prop at all.

Class 0x24's handler, and an Init rather than an update: it builds the actor and then installs one of six state routines as the object's own entry point. The parameter tail at obj+0x1390 carries everything -- tail+0x04 the character type into obj+0x1F4, tail+0x05 the state selector into obj+0x130C, tail+0x0A the motion into obj+0x1B4. obj+0x11C is an animation PHASE SEED, not hit points: -1 draws a random start frame, anything else starts the clock there, which is how a row of identical props avoids moving in lockstep. Selector 0 splits on tail+0x0C: zero gives SetPieceStateIdle, non-zero SetPieceStateHoldThenPlay.

The per-frame body every class-0x24 state ends with: pose the skeleton through FUN_00411090 and, if obj+0x1324 is zero, advance the motion frame at obj+0x194 by one. So obj+0x1324 is a FREEZE flag -- non-zero holds the pose. Also carries two hardcoded set-piece effects for character type 0x55 and an extra drawn asset (slot 0x1382) for type 0x53.

Class 0x24 selector 0: play the motion and wait to be removed. Every state shares that removal test -- obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 chooses between "g_script_flags[tail+0x06] is set" and "g_active_cam_path == tail+0x06 and g_cam_path_frame >= tail+0x08".

Class 0x24 selector 0 with tail+0x0C non-zero: count obj+0x1320 up to tail+0x0C frames, then install motion tail+0x0E through FUN_004119A0 and become SetPieceStateIdle. The one state where tail+0x0E is a motion id rather than a camera path.
Class 0x24 selector 1: plays from the start and freezes -- obj+0x1324 = 1 -- once g_active_cam_path reaches tail+0x0E at frame tail+0x10.

Class 0x24 selector 2: starts frozen (the Init sets obj+0x1324 = 1) and takes two cues. tail+0x12/tail+0x14 clears the freeze and starts it playing; tail+0x0E/tail+0x10 sets it again. Both are a camera path plus a frame threshold.

Class 0x24 selector 3: starts frozen and falls. Sub 0 zeroes the velocity, sub 1 integrates obj+0x5C -= 0.027222222, obj+0x50 += obj+0x5C, obj+0x44 += obj+0x50 until it reaches g_camera_fixed_eye_y, then clamps to the floor and clears the freeze so the animation plays. The same 0.027222222 half-gravity ActorArcVelocity uses. Freezes again on the motion's last frame, g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1.

Class 0x24 selector 4: slides. Sub 0 sets a 0x27-frame timer and a fixed velocity of (0.646266, 0, 0.613497); sub 1 adds it to obj+0x40/obj+0x48 each frame until the timer runs out; sub 2 waits a further 0x19 frames; sub 3 stops. Freezes on the motion's last frame.

Class 0x24 selector 5: holds until the motion frame passes 0x32, then drifts down under a much gentler 0.0034027777 until it reaches the ground plane. Unlike the other five its removal test has no script-flag variant -- it is always the camera path.

Class 0x25's handler, and an Init: it builds the actor and installs ScriptedHumanoidUpdate as the object's entry point. Everything comes from the parameter tail -- tail+0x00 the character type, tail+0x02/+0x04 the removal trigger (cam path and frame, or a script-flag index when obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 is set), tail+0x08 a model handle into obj+0x1304, and tail+0x0C a pointer to the COMMAND BLOCK. The block's header gives the opening motion at +0x04 and a phase seed at +0x06, -1 meaning rand()%10, and the commands start at +0x08. In Boss Mode character types 0x39 and 0x3A are remapped to the player's selected character through DAT_009A2242/DAT_009A2256. obj+0x124 is a per-character hit radius from the table at 0x004C4D28.

Class 0x25's bytecode VM, and the second-largest class in the game at 142 spawns. Walks 8-byte commands -- {s16 op, s16 mode, s16 a, s16 b}, or 16 bytes when the command carries a point -- running them until one blocks; a command that cannot proceed leaves the cursor where it is and falls through to the per-frame tail, so a run of setup commands all take effect in one frame and only a wait costs one. 19 opcodes: 0/1/4 wait on a condition (frame count, camera path+frame, motion frame, script flag, or closing on a point) -- and 0 and 1 differ in what they leave behind: obj+0x1324 is set to the OPCODE, and that word is the freeze flag the draw routine tests, so op 0 lets the animation run and op 1 holds the pose, 2/3 set the motion, 5/6/7 turn, 8 sets the position, 9 and 16 swap models from per-character tables, 10 skips an arm unless the player count matches, 11 rides an op_ object path through CamEvalObjectPath6 on the CAMERA's frame, 13 plays a sound, 14 sets the draw mode, 15 jumps, 17 hands the object to one of five other routines, 18 is ActorKill and -1 falls into the idle routine at LAB_00484D40. The per-frame tail runs the turn, the path follow and the draw.

Class 0x25's per-frame draw, called from the tail of every blocked command. Poses the skeleton through FUN_00411090 and then advances the motion frame at obj+0x194 only while obj+0x1324 is zero -- the same freeze flag class 0x24 has. It reads obj+0x1330 nowhere, so that field is not a draw mode whatever op 14 looks like. It also draws a per-spawn decoration chosen by tail+0x06: 1 and 2 are fixed props at hardcoded points, 3 rides an op_ object path, and 4 draws only while g_active_cam_path is 0x93.

Class 0x41's shared prologue: 25 of the update routines open with it. Despawns the prop when g_evt_step_index has CHANGED more than obj+0x11C times -- the counter is the step index, so this is a lifetime in event STEPS, not blocks -- and immediately when g_scene_index==1 and g_script_flags[0x77] is set. This is what makes obj+0x11C a LIFETIME IN EVENT STEPS -- PlaceGenericProp writes the descriptor's +0x11C to both this and obj+0x28C, and only types 5, 12 and 33 ever draw the slot.

Class 0x41 type 32, the lift. Script flag 0x37 holds obj+0x1A0 at g_camera_block_eye.y - 15, and stage 2 raises it over cp_st2 path 28 (slot 83), whose eye climbs 55.0 -> 144.2 -- an 89-unit vertical ride starting exactly at the spawn's Y of 40.0. Flags 0x6B and 0x6C fold the near and far pairs of cage leaves 0x200 BAMS a frame from 0x4000->0x8000 and 0x8000->0xC000, each playing COMMON\\DOORKICK3_22K_1.WAV on its first frame; obj+0x2A0 counts frames flag 0x6B has been up and releases an overhead panel (obj+0x1CC, 0->0x1000) after 0x27. Every angle test is < limit+1, so each hinge rests one step past the round number. Models are komono_suimon.bin entries 5/6/9 -- the FILE is named for the area, not for this object; rendered it is a folding lattice cage gate. Stage 2 places one, block 17 step 8.

Class 0x40. Allocates N HordeMemberInit objects of 0x13F4 into g_horde_members (0x007DCC20, 10 slots), each carrying its index at +0x131B and the placer's position, selector and count, then ActorKills itself. Selector obj+0x130C: 0 -> one member; 1 -> 8, or 10 in a two-player game, 6 in evt blocks 0x0E/0x12 (8 with two players) and 4 in block 0x19; 2 -> not a spawner at all, it calls FUN_0043DC30 and dies. Nine spawns, all selector 1.

One horde member's constructor, installed by PlaceHorde. Allocates a 0x504 side struct at obj+0x1390, fixes the character type at 0x1D (mol.bin, a six-segment chain) and picks the variant in side+0x68 from g_evt_block_index -- 3->0, 8->1, 0x0E->3, 0x12->4, 0x19->2. Seeds the member's place in the entry formation from g_horde_formation (0x0055E200) and its wander box from 0x0055E568/0x0055E574, increments both enemy counters unless the variant is 2, then installs HordeMemberUpdate.

The horde member's seven-state machine and draw. States: 0 hold, 1 fly the six-segment entry spline from g_horde_formation, 2 wind up, 3 dive at the camera, 4 pull out, 5 wander the box with neighbour avoidance inside 6.0 units, 6 dead. Dies to one shot for 80 points, playing STAGE1_SE or STAGE2_SE PDMG_MORR1/2_44.wav by g_scene_index; draws a ground shadow at slot 0x10D0 on g_camera_fixed_eye_y. Returns immediately while g_active_cam_path is 0x47.

PlaceGenericProp cases 0x46/0x47/0x48 call this to decide what an Original Mode collectible is. Walks up to 4 weighted entries of g_original_item_tables[g_scene_index] (stride 8, cumulative weights at +4..+7) against rand(); the chosen id goes to obj+0x290 and -1 means the prop draws nothing. The id then indexes g_original_item_records (0x005957D8, stride 0xC) for the two model slots at +0x00/+0x02, the draw scale at +0x04 and the pickup id at +0x08.

Draws an animated effect through EffectDrawTree with AssetDrawSlot. The argument is a 4-int state block {effect id, motion id, frame, prev frame} living inside the owning object -- obj+0x324 for a class-0x41 prop.
As EffectDrawUnlit but routes each part through SubmitSlotWithSceneLightArray instead of AssetDrawSlot. KindedPropUpdate picks this one for item set 4 and for scene 3.

Wraps the frame counter (to 0 at g_motion_play_length[motion]-1, and to the end when it goes negative) and then walks g_effect_trees[effect id]'s children with EffectDrawNode. The descriptor IS a node: same {u32 slot; s16 bone; u16 children; u32 child[]} struct, with slot 0 and bone 0 so the root itself never draws.

One effect node: push, EffectPoseNode, AssetDrawSlot(node->slot), recurse into the children, pop. A node with bone < 1 is a pure transform and draws nothing. Slot 0x10CE gets a random 0.27-0.37 scale each frame, which is how the smoke puffs vary.

The per-frame transform of one effect node: MatrixTranslate from EffectFrameTranslations, then RotZ/RotY/RotX from EffectFrameRotations, indexed by the node's bone - 1. g_effect_interp_mode[effect] selects the rate: 0 is one key per frame, otherwise the animation runs at half rate and odd frames blend the two neighbouring keys (mode 2 slerping through matrices when any axis differs by more than 0x3000).

Address of one frame's translation array inside the motion buffer: g_motion_slots[motion].base + 4 + frame * align4(bones * 0x12 - 0xF), then bone * 0xC for three floats. The effect's animation is an ordinary motion; only the node tree is its own.
Address of one frame's rotation array, the same stride as EffectFrameTranslations offset past the translations; bone * 6 for three BAMS shorts in X, Y, Z order.
atan2(|a x b|, a.b) for two vec3s, returned in BAMS. ComputeLookAtAngleError uses it to index the camera turn-rate curve, and TurnLookAtToward to size its slerp step.

dot(a,b)^2 / (|a|^2 * |b|^2), negated when the dot is negative -- the square of the cosine, never rooted. The camera hooks' `> 0.99999` convergence tests are against this value, so the threshold is about 0.18 degrees, not 0.26.
(num * b + den * a) / (num + den). CameraEaseBlockEyeToPathPose and CameraEaseEyeToPath call it with (1, 15) -- one sixteenth of the way from a to b per frame.

Eases g_camera_block_eye toward the deferred-rail pose eye at 0x009C70C0 by a sixteenth a frame while g_camera_ease_eye is set, and snaps straight to it otherwise. CameraTrackEnemiesTick opens with this.

Class 0x31 state 7, the hub. Plays the idle for the actor's current stance -- the ground picks a walk variant from g_class31_motion_sets, the three wall and ceiling stances have their own clips 0x138, 0x137 and 0x131 (0x20F, 0x20C and 0x212 for character type 0x18) -- turns toward the camera with TurnActorAwayFromPointTestArrival at 0x200 a frame, then offers state 0x1D (0x1E for character 0x18, the re-arm) to ThrowerTryEnterState and otherwise asks ThrowerPickNextState what to do next. An actor off the ground does not turn. Ends by emitting the movement trail with ThrowerEmitGroundDust(0x5A).

Class 0x31 state 8. Idles in the pose its stance names -- 0x129, 0x124 or 0x134 off the ground, the motion set's own idle pair on it -- until ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot succeeds, then plays sound 0x2416A9 and goes to state 9, the pounce, for character types 0x16, 0x18 and 0x19. Character 0x17 instead goes to state 0x20 when it is standing on surface 0x35 above the camera, else state 0x18.

Class 0x31 state 10, the leap back out of the player's face after a pounce. Picks a point 5 units to one side of the camera and 50 in front of it in the camera's yaw-only frame, traces a vertical segment there from y-1000 to y+1000 with ColiTraceSegmentAllSets and lands on what it hits -- falling back to g_camera_fixed_eye_y when the trace misses -- then arcs to it with ActorArcBeginToWaypoint under a three-stage arc motion script chosen by character type and stance. Plays the motion set's landing clip and returns to state 7 once 0x5A frames have passed or the actor is 50 units clear.

Class 0x31 state 11. Sub 0 records the start height in obj+0x1388, sets obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 and plays 0x1BC for character type 0x17 and 0x3A5 for everything else; sub 1 falls under obj+0x5C = -0.05444444 until QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+1.0, z) catches it, then picks a landing clip by the drop measured against g_coli_hit_y -- over 15 units the same long clip again, between 10 and 15 the short 0x1BA for type 0x17 and 0x3A9 otherwise, under 10 none at all -- and zeroes obj+0x1388 whenever it plays one, which is what lets sub 2 exit at once instead of waiting the fall clip out. Sub 2 goes to state 10 when obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 is set and state 7 otherwise; a dead actor, or any actor whose landing surface is 0x5A, is killed and routed to state 3 for character 0x16 or ThrowerEnterCorpseState for the rest.

Class 0x31 states 14, 15 and 16: the leap onto a wall or the ceiling. ThrowerFindWallBeside / ThrowerFindCeilingAbove have already put the destination in obj+0x13D8..E0; this begins the arc with ActorArcBeginToAtSpeed, installs the state's own three-stage arc motion script (g_class31_arc_to_wall_b for 14, g_class31_arc_to_wall_a for 15, g_class31_arc_to_ceiling for 16), plays sound 0x2416A9, and on arrival sets the stance bit its state id names -- 14 sets 0x80, 15 sets 0x40, 16 sets 0x100 in obj+0x136C -- plus 0x20, off the ground. Those bits are the stance that selects every later motion and attack row. Returns to state 7.

Class 0x31 state 17, and it is the decapitation recovery: only ThrowerShotFeedback's head-model swap sets the obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 that routes states 1 and 2 here. Sets obj+0x34 bit 0x100 -- the window in which shots ricochet -- plays motion 0x127 with a 5-frame fade for every character type, plays sound 0x1C17A9, and on the last frame clears both that bit and the knocked-down latch before asking ThrowerPickNextState. Character type 0x18 can never reach it, since ThrowerOnShot diverts it to state 0x21; and 0x127 is a szom.bin clip, so character type 0x17 -- the only one on kame.bin's skeleton -- asks here for a clip its own rig does not have. [open]

Class 0x31 state 18, an entrance. Plays the walk variant from g_class31_motion_sets[set] chosen by obj+0x34 bit 27, records the start position in obj+0x13C0..C8, and hands to state 7 once the 2D distance travelled reaches the float at descriptor tail +0x04. Stage 2 block 17 step 5 spawns two zstin this way with a distance of 15.0.

Class 0x31 state 19, an entrance. Plays the motion named by the int at descriptor tail +0x04 once -- 296 for every stage-2 zstin that uses it -- then plays sound 0x2916A9, sets obj+0x136C bit 0x80000 and hands to state 7.

Class 0x31 state 21, an entrance no shipped spawn uses and no state can reach -- cut content. Rides object path 0x14F (op_st2 local 7) at g_cam_path_frame for 0xC4 frames; both the slot and the count are immediates, not descriptor fields. Copies position and all three BAMS angles out of CamEvalObjectPath6 -- which returns three floats then three ints, whatever Ghidra's signature says -- holds obj+0x34 bit 0x100 while riding, then claims an attack permit, discards the answer, and goes to state 9.

Class 0x31 state 22, an entrance no shipped spawn uses and no state can reach -- dead code. When ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot fails it forces obj+0x121 from g_active_player -- 1 gives player 1, 2 a coin flip, 0 or -1 player 0 -- and attacks with no permit actually held. Draws obj+0x131A from g_class31_attack_picks, installs the arc script with ThrowerLoadAttackArcScript, and arcs to ThrowerPickLandingPoint over the s32 frame count at descriptor tail +0x04, calling ThrowerStrikeConnect every frame IsPlayerAttackable allows. Ends in state 10.

Class 0x31 state 23, both an entrance and an attack. Sets obj+0x1F8 bit 0x10 and plays the motion at descriptor tail +0x04 for the frame count at tail +0x08; then clears the bit, claims a permit, draws an attack index, and arcs from where it stands to ThrowerPickLandingPoint taken at g_camera_eye_y over that same count, rolling obj+0x6C back to level at 0xCCC a frame and calling ThrowerStrikeConnect every frame. Ends in state 25. Stage 2 block 21 step 2 spawns two zstin this way, motion 310 over 45 and 60 frames.

Class 0x31 state 24. Takes ThrowerPickLandingPoint as its target, draws an attack index, plays the g_class31_throws entry's approach clip until it is within that entry's own distance of the point, then plays its strike clip and calls ThrowerStrikeConnect on the frame the entry names. Ends in state 25.

Class 0x31 state 25, the retreat the two scripted attacks end in. Plays the motion set's landing clip and returns to state 7 once 0x5A frames have passed or the actor is more than 50 units from the camera -- 30 units and no clip test for character type 0x17, which also faces away from its strike anchor while it goes. Releases the permit with ThrowerReleaseAttackPermit on the way out.

Class 0x31 state 27, an entrance; four shipped spawns, all zslman in st5evtbl. Six sub-states over an 0x18-byte tail: three floats at +0x04 are the destination camera-relative offset of which only +0x08, the Y, is ever read; s16 +0x10 the camera path frame to drop on, matched against g_cam_path_frame or camera block 2's frame at 0x009A6458; s16 +0x12 the descent frames; s16 +0x14 the hold frames; s8 +0x16 the player to grab, -1 meaning at random. It anchors to the camera every frame, drops on the cue at obj+0x50 = dY/frames, blinks for the first fifteen hold frames, then takes g_attack_permits[p] outright with a two-player fallback, plays 0x1E5 or 0x1E7 at random and damages on obj+0x19C == 30. Subs 2 to 4 ride MatrixTranslate(camera eye) then MatrixRotateY(g_camera_yaw_bams + 0x8000) and write only X and Z; sub 5 tracks the camera by delta through obj+0x137C..0x1384. Sounds 0x2516A9 ENE_WALK2 on the cue frame and again at half the finish clip, 0x2916A9 ENE_WALK6 on landing, 0x1F23A9 LASER_SWORD on as the hold begins and 0x2023A9 LASER_SWORD off on every frame of the solid phase. The last pair is a looping pair from g_looping_se_ids / g_looping_se_stop_ids, so the off id calls SoundStopAllLoopingSe before playing; it still fires once per solid frame, which is the engine's own behaviour and not a dedupe.

Class 0x31 state 28, an entrance; six shipped spawns, all in trnevtbl. The tail is 0x0C bytes: s32 +0x04 the motion, played from rand() modulo its own length with a 4-frame blend; s16 +0x08 the condition -- 0 a frame count in obj+0x1330, 1 g_cam_path_frame, 2 g_script_flags -- and s16 +0x0A the operand. Then it jumps to the signed byte at tail +0x03, which is 7 in every shipped record. Any selector above 2 waits for ever.

Class 0x31 state 30. Waits for obj+0x136C bit 0x8000000 to clear, then puts both of character 0x18's weapons back -- bone 5's draw slot 0x1FF1 becomes 0x1FF3 and bone 8's 0x1FED becomes 0x1FEF, each with its hit sphere restored from PTR_DAT_004D032C -- and clears that arm's destroyed-zone bit. Returns to state 7.

Class 0x31 state 32. Plays motion 0x1B8, pins itself to where that clip ended, then loops: claim a permit if it has none, draw an attack index, play its strike clip calling ThrowerStrikeConnect, then the motion set's second idle for 0x78 frames, and strike again. It never leaves the state.

Class 0x31 state 33, the shot reaction character type 0x18 takes instead of the stumble. Sub 0 picks the knock clip by stance -- 0x215 ground, 0x1FE and 0x1F4 the two walls, 0x206 ceiling -- fades it over 5 frames on a fresh knock or hard-cuts it on a re-entry (obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, which also skips the velocity clear and counts obj+0x1328 up), launches ThrowerBeginKnockbackArc while obj+0x1328 is under 2, and calls SelectActorGravityAxis. Then it rides the arc and bounces off whichever of the six axes obj+0x1354 names, standing 4.5 units off a wall, negating that axis by -0.5 and halving the other two, playing sound 0x2716A9 each time, until the speed on that axis drops to 0.15 or obj+0x1338 reaches 0x78. Landing waits (rand()%10+1)*3 frames, plays the stance's get-up clip -- 0x216 / 0x1FF / 0x1F5 / 0x207 -- and returns to state 7 with obj+0x133C = 0x14, a 20-frame window in which shots do nothing. A dead actor, or surface 0x5A under it, goes to ThrowerEnterCorpseState instead.

Class 0x31 state 34, an entrance; eight shipped spawns, all zslman in st6evtbl, covering all four surface stances. A three-hop blinking materialisation, not a retreat -- the earlier name ThrowerStateBackAwayThreeUnits was wrong. After the s32 delay at descriptor tail +0x04 it hops to origin + RotY(obj+0x68) * (0, 0, obj+0x1348 * 30) with obj+0x1348 counting 3, 2, 1, so 90 then 60 then 30 units from the origin it captured at entry, 30 frames apart -- obj+0x1344 is set to 30.0 and decremented on the hop frame itself -- blinking obj+0x138C and obj+0x136C bit 2 on g_frame_counter parity throughout. The stance idle is an immediate rather than a table lookup: 0x208 ground, 0x1FD, 0x1F3 and 0x205 by obj+0x136C bit6 + bit7*2 + bit8*3. It ends on sound 0x2225A9 STAGE6_SE MONITOR3, goes solid, and jumps to tail +0x03. EnemyThrowerInit special-cases this state for character type 0x18, starting it invisible.

Class 0x31 state 1, the stumble. Clamps obj+0x1368 -- which ThrowerOnShot set to the bone index -- to 15, looks the group up in g_bone_reaction_group and the motion in g_class31_hit_reactions[set], and cross-fades it over 0x14 frames for bones under 9 or hard-sets it for 9 and above, so a leg shot cuts where an arm shot blends. On the clip's last frame it clears obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 and obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, then goes to state 17 if obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 is set -- which only a decapitation sets -- and otherwise asks ThrowerPickNextState.

Class 0x31's next-state router, called from states 7, 1 and 17. Dispatches on the ground distance to the camera: d <= 30 (15 for character type 0x17 standing on surface 0x35) goes to state 8; otherwise the band is 1 for 40 < d <= 50 and 2 everywhere else, and it draws a candidate state from g_class31_action_picks[set][band][(rand()>>4)%10 + (obj+0x1318 & 7)*10] and offers it to ThrowerTryEnterState, latching obj+0x135C and obj+0x136C bit 0x2000 on success and falling back to state 7 on refusal. Band 0 of the table is never reached and the band != 0 test is dead code.

Gate for a proposed class-0x31 state on the current actor; writes obj+0x1310 and obj+0x1312 and returns 1 only if it is legal. 7 always; 8 only when ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot FAILS and 9 only when it succeeds; 0xC and 0xD need a permit and refuse character type 0x18; 0xE and 0xF need obj+0x136C bit 0x20 clear and a successful ThrowerFindWallBeside at -1.0 or +1.0; 0x10 needs bit 0x20 clear and ThrowerFindCeilingAbove; 0x1D and 0x1E only from state 7 and only when ThrowerHasBareHand; 0x1F needs ThrowerBothHandsArmed plus a permit; 0x20 needs a permit and ground surface 0x35; everything else returns 0.

Class 0x31's strike connect, run every frame of an attack state. Tests no range at all. Picks the 32-bit table g_class31_melee_attacks[set] entry obj+0x131A + obj+0x1364*4, or g_class31_throws entry obj+0x131A when obj+0x136C bit 0x400 is set, fires when obj+0x19C equals the entry's hit frame -- or, in the 32-bit table, when that frame is -1 and the arc has reached phase 4 -- passes the cancel-mask test (obj+0x1318 & mask & 7) != mask, then calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, kind, the entry's player motion) and latches obj+0x136C bit 0x800. kind is 1 normally and 0 when obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 is set, in which case the actor despawns immediately after the hit.
Frees g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] and sets obj+0x121 to 0xFF; if obj+0x136C bit 0x8000 is set it also clears it and zeroes g_attack_committed, the global that short-circuits TryClaimAttackSlot.
Decrements g_enemies_alive exactly once per actor, guarded by obj+0x136C bit 0x800000.
Decrements g_enemies_present exactly once per actor, guarded by obj+0x136C bit 0x1000000.

Runs when obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 is set or the hit points at obj+0x11C fall below 1: unless this is the last enemy present it sets obj+0x34 bit 0x10000 and frees the tracking slot g_enemy_slots[obj+0x120*8], then always calls ThrowerRetireFromAliveCount.

Puts the actor into its corpse state: clears obj+0x136C bits 0x180000, sets obj+0x34 bits 0xC001 (bit 14 freezes the motion advance), retires from g_enemies_present unless obj+0x38 bit 0, steps the motion play cursor back one frame, then enters state 5 for character type 0x18 and state 4 otherwise.

Launches the death knockback from ThrowerStateFallAndLand sub 0. t = clamp((15.0 / the length of obj+0x70..0x78) * 10.0, 0, inf), times 1.5 when obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 is set; the actor's view-space sphere centre pulled t units nearer the camera and transformed back through the current camera matrix becomes the arc target, keeping the actor's own y for character type 0x18 with obj+0x136C bits 0xC0. So the body flies at the camera, harder the nearer it already is.

Effect emitter keyed by a code. 0x46, from the ground bounce, is one-shot per bounce on obj+0x136C bit 0x4000 and spawns sprite 0x61 in rain or on surfaces 0x37 and 0x05 and sprite 0x46 otherwise, oriented to g_coli_hit_normal. 0x50, from an arc landing, needs obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000 clear and bit 0x20000000 set and spawns sprite 0x4B scaled 0.4, 2.0, 0.2. 0x50 and 0x5A then share a movement trail for character type 0x16 that spawns two sprites at the midpoint of obj+0x13E4..EC and the current position, sized by distance * 0.05981133 with scale 0.8 and 0.2, at +0x4000 and +0x8000 BAMS.

Whether an enemy may commit an attack on a player. False unless the major scene state copy at 0x009C6F08 is 2; true when g_app_state is 5; otherwise the per-player state word at 0x009A5C62 + player*0x98 must be 5, the value the spawn-into-play rows of the table at 0x00579DE8 install. TryClaimAttackSlot voids a permit it has just picked when this returns 0.

Copies the current attack's arc motion script into the actor's slot. The stance row is bit6 + 2*(bit7 + 2*bit17) + 3*bit8 of obj+0x136C, the entry is g_class31_melee_attacks[obj+0x130C] + (obj+0x131A + row*4)*0x10, and the pointer at that entry's +0x00 is copied as 12 dwords into g_arc_scripts at 0x009C8AA0 + obj+0x3C*0x30.

Returns the bone index of the hand still holding a weapon: 5 for the right (draw slot obj+0x4DC) or 8 for the left (obj+0x68C), 0 if neither. The armed part ids are 0x1FA2 and 0x1F9E for character type 0x16 and 0x1FF3 and 0x1FEF for 0x18; every other type returns 0. When both hands are armed a rand() parity test picks which one wins.

True when one of character 0x16's or 0x18's hands has thrown its weapon and the other has not been restored -- the gate on states 0x1D and 0x1E, the re-arm. Character types 0x17 and 0x19 have no weapon and always fail it.
True when character 0x16 or 0x18 still holds a weapon in either hand -- the gate on state 0x1F, the throw. Character types 0x17 and 0x19 always fail it, which is why zstin never throws.

Where a class-0x31 actor on a wall or ceiling should be standing. Quantises the actor's yaw to the nearest cardinal within 0x2000, builds a probe pair from the stance bits in obj+0x136C -- 0x80 one wall, 0x40 the other, 0x100 the ceiling, which also pitches the probe by 0xC000 -- and traces between them with ColiTraceSegmentAllSets. Returns 1 and writes the contact point when it is within 10 units (15 on the ceiling); otherwise it sends the actor to state 11 to fall, or to state 8 if it is still attached.

The gate on class-0x31 states 14 and 15. Refuses unless the actor is facing the camera within 0x2000 and obj+0x136C bit 1 is clear, then traces horizontally from a point 60 units to the actor's own left (argument -1.0) or right (+1.0), at the ground height under it plus rand()%20 + 9.0, back to the actor. On a hit it stores a point 4.5 units short of the wall in obj+0x13D8..E0 and returns 1 -- so with no wall there, the actor simply does not go.
The gate on class-0x31 state 16. Traces from 1000 units above the actor in its own frame down to the actor, and on a hit stores the contact point in obj+0x13D8..E0 and returns 1.

Class 0x31's per-bone draw callback, installed into obj+0x12EC by EnemyThrowerInit. Aims bone 2 at the camera through FUN_00453BE0, then draws the part id from g_skeleton_node_out. Character type 0x18's parts 0x1FED and 0x1FF1 grow a companion piece by 0.025 a frame clamped at 1.0 under a Y-only scale; part 0x1FB9 ping-pongs a morph weight over 120 frames at 1/60 a frame; parts 0x2016 and 0x204A cycle 0x2017 and 0x204B plus the global frame counter modulo 0x32. The 0x1FF0 arm is unreachable -- the guard admits only 0x1FED and 0x1FF1 but the branch compares against 0x1FEE -- so 0x1FF4 is always drawn.

The alternate obj+0x12EC draw hook, installed by EnemyThrowerInit when g_GameMode and DAT_009C88A8 are both 1 (item code 0x15) alongside doubling obj+0x3A4. Draws nothing while DAT_009C88A8 is clear, and wraps ThrowerDrawBonePart in a 2x scale for bone 2 only.

Thunk to ActorSetMotionBlended on the current actor's motion block. Its first argument is read but never used, so it always drives DAT_009A26A0 + 0x194; every caller passes obj+0x194 anyway. The third argument is a start frame inside the clip, not a blend length.
Zeroes the current actor's acceleration (+0x58/5C/60) and then its velocity (+0x4C/50/54).

Copies a 12-dword three-stage arc motion script -- {s32 motion, s32 start frame, s32 fade, s32 threshold} x 3 -- into g_arc_scripts at 0x009C8AA0, stride 0x30, indexed by the actor's enemy slot obj+0x3C. ActorArcStep plays stage 0 at the start of the arc, stage 1 once the clip frame passes threshold [3], stage 2 once it passes [7], and reports the arc finished past [11]. Every script in the program names the same motion in all three stages, so a script is one clip cut into windup, flight and landing.

ActorArcBegin whose duration it works out itself: the horizontal distance at a fixed 30 world units per minFrames, where minFrames is 10 when obj+0x136C bit 0x2000000 is set and obj+0x34 bits 0x44000000 are not, else 15 -- so 2.0 or 3.0 units a frame -- clamped up to minFrames. ActorArcBeginToWaypoint uses this instead of ActorArcBeginTo for character type 0x19.

One frame of an arc, as an absolute position rather than an integration: x and z lerp from obj+0x13C0..C8 to obj+0x13CC..D4 over obj+0x1334, and y adds (T*T*0.027222222 + 2*dy)*n/(2T) - 0.027222222*n*n*0.5. Advances obj+0x1330 by the step and returns 0 once it passes the duration.

Where the surface an actor is stuck to actually is. Snaps the actor's yaw to the nearest cardinal within 0x2000, picks the probe axis from obj+0x136C -- 0x80 one wall, 0x40 the other, 0x100 the ceiling, none of them the floor -- and traces 1000 units (1500 for the ceiling) along it to a point 20 units past the actor. Writes the contact point and returns 1; on a miss with no ceiling bit it returns the actor's own x and z at g_camera_fixed_eye_y, and otherwise 0 with the out vector untouched.

Sets obj+0x1354, the arc kind ActorArcVelocity switches on: 0 floor, 1 ceiling, 2 wall at +X, 3 wall at -X, 4 wall at -Z, 5 wall at +Z. Derived from the cardinal-snapped yaw and obj+0x136C bits 0x40, 0x80 and 0x100, and it agrees with the acceleration ThrowerStateKnockedTumbling writes on the same axis.

TurnActorAwayFromPoint that also reports arrival: steps obj+0x68 at most the step argument in BAMS toward the heading atan2(obj - point), then returns FUN_0040A040(new yaw, target, tolerance) -- 1 when the yaw is now within the tolerance of the target. Ghidra types it void; the value falls through EAX. ThrowerStateStandAndDecide calls it with step and tolerance both 0x200 and uses both senses: non-zero advances the sub-state, and later not-1 resets it.

Traces a vertical segment from (x, y-1000, z) up to (x, y, z) and returns g_coli_hit_surface -- the surface-type id, 0 for a miss. The sibling of QueryGroundHeightAt, which returns the height. Callers test 0x35, 0x37, 5 and 0x5A.

On DAT_009C8E98 == 6 only, spawns a 120-frame flat ground ring at the actor's shadow anchor obj+0x100/+0x108 and the ground height plus 0.05. Draws asset slot 0x1A38 scaled in X and Z only, expanding from 0 to 4x over its life through cos at 136.5333 BAMS a frame.

Stretches an installed arc motion script onto obj+0x1334 for every character type but 0x19. slack = duration - script[10] - script[6] - script[7] + script[5]; with room to spare it grows both stages' fade lengths (indices 6 and 10) a frame at a time until they fill it, clamping each at 0x7F, and when it is tight it walks stage 1's start frame up and its threshold down until the three stages fit. Called from ActorArcStep phase 0.

The same fit for character type 0x19, and it moves start frames rather than fades. slack = duration - script[10] - script[6] - script[7] + script[5] and k = (int)(|slack| * 0.5): a positive slack adds k to both fade lengths and puts the remainder on stage 1's, a negative one advances stage 1's and stage 2's start frames (indices 5 and 9) by k, each clamped at its own threshold, and puts the remainder on stage 1's -- so a short leap skips into the middle of the clip rather than playing it slowly. Ghidra drops the FPU argument to __ftol; the 0.5 is float ptr 0x004C43AC = 0x3F000000.

Stage-1 opening vehicle (car_pl.bin + char_adv00.bin occupants). Picks its route from g_active_cam_path: cp_st1 0/1 (0x20/0x21) ride op_st1 0/1 at min(g_cam_path_frame, g_cam_path_length[slot]); cp_st1 1 clears the moving flag obj+0x1320 past frame 0x15D and stops re-evaluating. cp_st1 2 (0x22) does NOT ride a path -- it parks the car with CamEvalObjectPath6(0xFE, 350.0), a literal, and reads op_st1 2 (0xFF) only for rot_y, which becomes obj+0x1334, the occupants' yaw, minus 0x4000. obj+0x1330 gains 0x2000 a frame while moving and spins the two wheel pairs.

Class 0x31's copy of ActorShotFeedback. Forces g_hit_result to 5 while obj+0x34 bit 0x100 is set, so a downed thrower only ricochets.
